title: Generator test, second version: a line chain that knows where a paragraph opens and whose table drifts, against all established facts
statement: R-008 (a line-restarting glyph chain with the line end as a symbol, plus copying of nearby words) reproduced 7 of 8 established facts on the hidden pages and missed F-008 (words opening with p or f gather on paragraph first lines). It cannot reproduce F-008 in the present attack format: the scorer lays the attacker's lines onto the hidden pages in order, so no text can know which of its lines will open a paragraph. A code change in review (branch code-R-paragraph-aware-attack-fleet-fable) lets attack.json carry first_lines, the lines a procedure wrote as a paragraph's first line. With that change, on the public practice split, one procedure reproduces all 8 established facts and two facts awaiting a verdict: the same chain (four symbols of context, word space and line end as symbols) with (a) a second opening symbol for a paragraph's first line, (b) a table that drifts, each stretch of 60 lines written from the whole-text table at half weight plus a moving window of 12 public pages, and (c) one word in ten copied from the last ten words with one glyph altered in context. No rule names a glyph or a fact. Practice values, generator against manuscript: F-001 13.4 / 61.6, F-002 0.230 / 0.230, F-003 39.7 / 54.6, F-004 0.303 / 0.325, F-005 0.244 / 0.230, F-006 4.68 / 4.83, F-007 0.179 / 0.210, F-008 7.5 / 15.4 (threshold 3), line-break gap in edge dependence 0.196 / 0.173, within-page word reuse 0.183 / 0.311 (passes its shuffle test, but far below the manuscript's level). One seed, one setting, no search over settings; F-001 is the thin margin (threshold 10). Weak points to work on: page-level reuse is well below the manuscript's, and nothing here is scored on hidden pages. Proposed: once first_lines is merged, send this as the next generator test (one per contributor per day), and separately as the fact attack on F-008.
check: attack.json {"attack": "generator", "cut": "lines", "lines": [...], "first_lines": [...]} after the first_lines code change is merged; the record shows k of n
